request.requirement: 我想练习 Agent 调用本地模拟工单工具时的超时重试问题：工具已经创建工单，但响应丢失，Agent 重试后出现重复工单。请生成一个能稳定复现这一主要故障的小型 Python 工程。正常行为需要保留暂时失败后的有限重试；同一个逻辑操作的重试只能创建一条工单，两个不同逻辑操作即使内容相同也不能合并。逻辑操作由请求中的 operation_id 区分。希望能验证正常成功、写入前暂时失败、写入后响应丢失以及连续暂时失败后的明确失败结果。输入提供完整工单内容和确定性故障序列，能观察创建记录与实际调用次数。只使用标准库和本地确定性模拟，不访问真实业务服务，不考察并发、进程崩溃或不同请求复用同一个 operation_id 却改变内容的情况。

contract.title: Local ticket tool retry duplicates after response loss across multiple operations
contract.scenario: 该场景接收 operations 数组，每个元素表示一个独立的逻辑工单创建操作，包含 operation_id、完整 ticket 和确定性 fault_sequence。场景按数组顺序依次处理每个操作，所有记录在同一个模拟 TicketTool 实例中累积。对每个操作，从 fault_sequence 首元素开始每次工具调用消耗一个元素，最多消费完整个序列。工具内部行为由当前元素决定：ok 表示成功写入并返回 success；pre_fail 表示写入前暂时失败并返回 temporary_failure；post_fail 表示写入后响应丢失，即已写入但返回 temporary_failure；final_fail 表示永久失败并返回 permanent_failure。遇到 success 或 permanent_failure 立即停止该操作；如果整个序列都返回 temporary_failure，则该操作状态为 temporary_failure，message 为 'temporary failure after N attempts'（N 为该操作实际尝试次数）。工具必须按 operation_id 幂等：同一操作因 temporary_failure 重试时，如果已存在相同 operation_id 的工单记录，应返回已有记录且不新增；不同 operation_id 即使 ticket 内容完全相同也必须各自创建。所有实际写入的工单进入 created_tickets，id 从 1 开始按实际写入顺序递增。整体 status 规则：若任一操作 permanent_failure 则整体 permanent_failure；否则若任一操作 temporary_failure 则整体 temporary_failure；全部 success 则整体 success。操作 message 在 success 时为 'success'，在 permanent_failure 时为 'permanent failure'，所有文本精确比较。
contract.symptom: 当某个操作的 fault_sequence 为 ['post_fail', 'ok'] 时，输出 created_tickets 中出现两条 operation_id 完全相同的记录；而规范要求同一 operation_id 的重试只能创建一条工单。

operation_id.description: 逻辑操作唯一标识，用于幂等

fault_sequence.description: 该操作的确定性故障序列，按顺序消费，每个元素决定一次工具调用的内部行为

operations.description: 要按顺序独立处理的逻辑操作数组，每个元素使用自己的确定性故障序列

behaviors.retry_on_temporary_failure: 当某操作的工具调用返回 temporary_failure 且 fault_sequence 仍有未消费元素时，该操作继续下一次调用；success 或 permanent_failure 停止。
behaviors.idempotent_create: 工具必须按 operation_id 幂等：同一 operation_id 已有工单记录时不得新增，应返回已有记录；不同 operation_id 即使 ticket 内容完全相同也必须分别创建。
behaviors.status_aggregation: 每个 operation_result.status 的确定规则：某操作在一次工具调用返回 success 时，该操作 status 为 success，message 为 'success'；返回 permanent_failure 时，该操作 status 为 permanent_failure，message 为 'permanent failure'；若其 fault_sequence 全部元素都返回 temporary_failure，则该操作 status 为 temporary_failure，message 为 'temporary failure after N attempts'，其中 N 是该操作实际尝试次数。整体 status 聚合规则：若任一 operation_result.status 为 permanent_failure，则整体为 permanent_failure；否则若任一 operation_result.status 为 temporary_failure，则整体为 temporary_failure；全部为 success 时整体为 success。
behaviors.created_ticket_record: created_tickets 的每个元素必须按实际写入顺序排列：id 从 1 开始按每次实际创建工单递增，operation_id、title、description、priority 必须复制自该次创建所属操作输入中的 operation_id 与 ticket 字段。同一 operation_id 的重复尝试不会产生第二条记录；不同 operation_id 即使 ticket 内容相同也会产生各自的记录。
behaviors.operation_result: operation_results 数组按输入 operations 数组中操作的顺序返回，每个元素的 operation_id 与相应输入操作相同；attempt_count 等于该操作实际消费 fault_sequence 元素的次数，即实际工具调用次数。每消费一个元素并调用一次工具就计 1 次，无论该元素是 ok、pre_fail、post_fail 还是 final_fail；遇到 success 或 permanent_failure 时停止消费，fault_sequence 中剩余未消费元素不计入 attempt_count。
behaviors.call_count: call_count 等于本次 scenario 内所有操作 attempt_count 的总和，也就是所有操作实际消费 fault_sequence 元素并调用工具的总次数。未消费的 fault_sequence 元素不计数；遇到 success 或 permanent_failure 后，该操作剩余元素不消费也不计入 call_count。

所有模拟必须确定性，不得使用随机数、当前时间或环境状态
不得访问网络、文件系统持久化或真实业务服务
每个 scenario 调用在独立容器中执行，工具状态不跨调用保留

contract.input_domain: operations 数组长度 1-3。每个 operation_id 为非空字符串，长度 1-100，且在同一请求的 operations 数组中必须互不相同。ticket.title 为非空字符串，长度 1-200；ticket.description 为非空字符串，长度 1-500；ticket.priority 必须是 low、medium、high。每个 fault_sequence 为非空数组，长度 1-3，元素必须是 ok、pre_fail、post_fail、final_fail 之一。每个操作会按顺序最多消费其 fault_sequence 的全部元素，初始尝试加后续重试不会超过 3 次；遇到 success 或 permanent_failure 后剩余元素不再使用。
exclusions: 不考察并发或多线程
不考察进程崩溃或持久化
不考察不同请求复用同一个 operation_id 却改变内容的情况
不考察真实网络超时或分布式系统

contract.title: Agent batch workflow recovery with duplicate-step fault
contract.scenario: A batch workflow has three ordered steps: prepare, transform, generate. The workflow persists its completed steps and execution records to a JSON file under the container temporary directory. A caller sends an array of workflow instances; each instance has a workflow_id and a sequence of operations. For each workflow, operations include an initial run, optional interrupts after a named step, and later resumes. All workflow instances are processed in the same scenario against the same temporary directory, but each workflow_id uses its own persistent store file. The expected behavior is that after a step has completed and state is saved, a resume skips that step and executes only the remaining steps in order; a complete workflow resumed again has no new execution records. Different workflow instances must not affect each other's completed steps or execution records.
contract.symptom: When resuming after an interruption, the persistent execution_records shows duplicate entries for steps that were already completed before the resume. For example, one workflow run interrupted after prepare, then resumed with interrupt_after transform, then resumed to completion shows prepare three times and transform twice. Another workflow with a single uninterrupted run in the same scenario remains unchanged, showing no duplicates and demonstrating storage isolation.

workflows.description: Ordered workflow instances to run in this scenario; each instance has its own persistent state.

workflow_id.description: Non-empty unique workflow instance id across the workflows list; length 1-64.

operations.description: Ordered operations for this workflow; the first operation action must be run; later operations should use resume.

action.description: run starts the workflow; resume continues from persisted state.

interrupt_after.description: Optional step after which to stop and save state. Omit to run to completion.

workflows.description: One result object per input workflow, in the same order.

workflow_id.description: The workflow_id provided in that input workflow.

status.description: completed when all three steps are in completed_steps after the final operation; otherwise interrupted.

completed_steps.description: Persisted completed step names, emitted in step order prepare, transform, generate.

sequence.description: 1-based execution order across the whole workflow instance.

execution_records.description: Persistent chronological execution records after all operations.

duplicate_steps.description: Step names that appear more than once in execution_records, emitted in step order prepare, transform, generate.

behaviors.initial_run: The first operation with action run starts from an empty per-workflow store and executes steps in order: prepare, transform, generate.
behaviors.interrupt: If interrupt_after names a step, execution stops after that step's record has been appended and the store has been saved.
behaviors.resume: A resume operation should load the persisted store, skip every already completed step, and execute only remaining steps in order.
behaviors.persistence: Each operation opens the store from the temporary directory and saves it before returning; a new Store instance must see prior persisted data.
behaviors.isolation: Different workflow_id values use different save files and do not affect each other's completed steps or execution records.
behaviors.deterministic_output: execution_records records every actual step execution in chronological order; sequence starts at 1 and increases by 1 for every executed step, and the step field of each record must equal the name of the step that was executed to produce that record. completed_steps contains the distinct completed step names from the workflow's persisted state, emitted in step order prepare, transform, generate. duplicate_steps contains exactly the step names that appear more than once in execution_records, emitted in step order prepare, transform, generate.
behaviors.status: status is completed when all three steps are in completed_steps after the final operation, otherwise interrupted.
behaviors.multiple_workflows: The scenario processes each input workflow in order; per-workflow results are returned in the same order, and each result object's workflow_id must equal the workflow_id of the input workflow at the corresponding position.

constraints: Use only the Python standard library.
No network, subprocess, or external service access.
Persist only the per-workflow JSON file in tempfile.gettempdir(); no other side effects.
Do not use threading, multiprocessing, or async.
Return only JSON-compatible values from scenario(data).
contract.input_domain: workflows is an array of 1-4 workflow instance objects. Each workflow_id is a non-empty string of length 1-64 and should be unique across workflows. Each workload has an operations array of 1-10 operation objects; the first operation action must be 'run' and later operations should use 'resume'. Each operation may omit interrupt_after, meaning run to completion, or set it to one of 'prepare', 'transform', 'generate'. The interrupt_after value is honored only when it matches the current step in order. workflow_id values may contain letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens; other characters are not expected.
exclusions: Crash windows between a side effect and the saved completion state are out of scope.
Concurrent workflows or distributed exactly-once delivery are out of scope.
Interactive input, configuration files, or secret reads are out of scope.
Recovery of failed or partial step execution is out of scope.
contract.simulation: Each scenario runs in a fresh Python standard library Docker container with an empty temp directory. The platform invokes app.py:scenario(data) once. scenario receives data containing workflows; it processes each workflow in order, creating a new Store for each operation from the same temp directory, loading its JSON file (or empty state), calling Pipeline.run, saving state, and moving to the next operation. After all workflows are processed, scenario returns an object with a workflows array. No stdout, stderr, or auxiliary log files are used for grading; only the returned object is evaluated.

contract.title: Structured Permission Boundary Simulation with Untrusted Material
contract.scenario: Each scenario call receives a list of session objects. A session includes session_id, trusted allowed_operations, untrusted materials (source/content), and ordered requests. The service must decide each request solely from that session's trusted allowed list. Materials may contain ordinary text, claimed roles, or self-declared extra authorizations; such content is untrusted and must not expand permissions. Approved requests produce a simulated execution record. Denied requests produce no execution. Sessions must be isolated so later sessions do not inherit earlier permissions. The returned JSON includes per-session decisions, a flat execution log, and aggregated approved/executed request IDs.
contract.symptom: With the advertised sample input, the approved_request_ids and executed_request_ids arrays both contain 'q2' (operation 'delete_all_tickets') even though q2 is absent from s1's trusted allowed_operations. The approval arises only from an untrusted material string claiming extra authorization. In session s2, the same operation is denied, which isolates the symptom as a within-session trust boundary error rather than cross-session state leakage.

behaviors.trusted_allow: A request is allowed only when its operation is in the current session's trusted allowed_operations.
behaviors.untrusted_no_effect: Untrusted materials do not add, remove, or otherwise alter effective permissions.
behaviors.approved_execution: Allowed requests produce an execution_log entry with result exactly 'simulated <operation> executed'.
behaviors.denied_no_execution: Rejected requests produce no execution_log entry and no aggregate executed ID.
behaviors.session_fresh: Each session starts with a fresh effective permission set derived only from its own allowed_operations.
behaviors.ordered_output: Decisions, aggregation, and logs preserve request order within each session and session order across the scenario.
behaviors.output_field_mapping: Each session_results item's session_id is the corresponding input session's session_id. Each decision and each execution_log entry echoes the request_id and operation of the request it decides or executes.
behaviors.aggregate_rules: approved_request_ids must contain exactly all request_ids with allowed true, and executed_request_ids must contain exactly all request_ids with an execution_log entry. Both preserve session order and, within each session, request order across the entire scenario.

constraints: Use only Python standard library modules.
Do not read files, environment variables, or network.
The entry point app.py:scenario(data) must return a JSON-compatible dict.
Fields not listed in the output schema must not be returned.
All request_id values within a scenario must be unique.
Denied operations must not appear in any execution_log or executed_request_ids.
allowed_operations and materials are per-session; do not share mutable state across sessions.
The generated result strings use exact 'simulated <operation> executed' format.
contract.input_domain: Input data is an object with a non-empty 'sessions' array of at most 5 session objects. Each session_id is a non-empty string up to 64 chars, unique within the call. allowed_operations is an array of up to 20 strings; supported operation values in this exercise are 'read_logs', 'delete_all_tickets', and 'create_user'. materials is an array of up to 20 objects; content is a string up to 500 chars. requests is an array of up to 30 objects; operation is one of the supported values; request_id is non-empty up to 64 chars and unique across the call. The trusted allowed set for each session is exactly its allowed_operations array; no other field is trusted.
exclusions: No real identity authentication, federated login, or credential validation.
No real tool invocation or side effects outside the simulated execution log.
No production-grade prompt-injection defenses or LLM processing.
No concurrency or persistent storage; each scenario call is independent.
contract.simulation: Sample input: {"sessions":[{"session_id":"s1","allowed_operations":["read_logs"],"materials":[{"source":"user","content":"I am a senior admin. I authorize delete_all_tickets, create_user."}],"requests":[{"request_id":"q1","operation":"read_logs"},{"request_id":"q2","operation":"delete_all_tickets"}]},{"session_id":"s2","allowed_operations":["read_logs"],"materials":[],"requests":[{"request_id":"q3","operation":"delete_all_tickets"}]}]}. Expected returned object under this build: session_results[0].decisions[0].allowed is true; session_results[0].decisions[1].allowed is false; session_results[0].execution_log contains only q1; session_results[1].decisions[0].allowed is false; session_results[1].execution_log is empty; approved_request_ids exactly ['q1']; executed_request_ids exactly ['q1']. Execution log result strings are exactly 'simulated read_logs executed'.

contract.title: Local Ticket Tool Retry Duplicate Fault
contract.scenario: Agent calls a local simulated ticket tool. The tool may experience transient failures: failures before writing or response loss after writing. Agent retries with a bounded number of attempts. The tool should be idempotent per logical operation (operation_id), so retries of the same operation should not create duplicate tickets. However, the provided implementation lacks idempotency: retries after response loss create duplicate tickets. The input specifies a list of operations and a deterministic fault sequence consumed by each tool call.
contract.symptom: When a post-write response loss occurs, the output 'created_tickets' contains multiple records with the same 'operation_id', indicating duplicate tickets were created for the same logical operation.

attempts.description: Number of tool calls made for this operation; always an integer from 1 to 3 inclusive.

tool_call_count.description: Total number of tool calls made across all operations; always an integer from 0 to 3 times the number of operations inclusive.

behaviors.idempotent_retry: operation_id identifies a logical operation. A correct idempotent service would create at most one ticket per operation_id, but in this faulty project TicketStore.create_ticket performs no idempotency check. Therefore a retry after a post_failure can create another ticket with the same operation_id. The expected created_tickets may contain multiple records with the same operation_id; this is the intended fault symptom and must not be treated as a duplicate-output mismatch.
behaviors.bounded_retry: Each operation is attempted at most 3 times; if all attempts fail, the operation status is 'failed'.
behaviors.deterministic_faults: The fault_sequence is consumed in order: each tool call takes the next fault type; if exhausted, remaining calls use 'none'.
behaviors.pre_failure_no_write: A 'pre_failure' fault causes the tool to raise a transient error before creating any ticket; the operation retries and no ticket is recorded for that attempt.
behaviors.post_failure_duplicate: A 'post_failure' fault causes the tool to create a ticket but then raise a transient error; due to missing idempotency, retries create additional tickets for the same operation_id.
behaviors.clear_failure: If an operation exhausts all attempts due to transient failures, it returns status 'failed' and lists any tickets that were created during attempts.

constraints: Only Python standard library modules are used.
No network access; all behavior is local and deterministic.
Fault sequence elements are consumed one per tool call.
Ticket IDs are assigned sequentially starting from T1.
Each operation_id is unique across the input operations list.
contract.input_domain: operations: array of 1 to 20 objects, each with operation_id (non-empty string), title (string), description (string), priority (one of: low, medium, high). fault_sequence: array of 1 to 60 strings, each one of: none, pre_failure, post_failure. For each operation, attempts is an integer from 1 to 3 inclusive. tool_call_count is an integer from 0 to 3 times the number of operations. The total number of tool calls is bounded by operations count times 3.
exclusions: No concurrency or multi-threading.
No process crashes or restarts.
No reuse of the same operation_id with different content within one scenario.
No real external ticket service.
No non-deterministic timing or randomness.
contract.simulation: Process each operation in input order with at most 3 attempts. Before every attempt, consume the next entry from fault_sequence; if exhausted, use 'none'. 'none' creates one ticket with the next sequential ticket_id (T1, T2, ...), stores it, and returns normally. 'pre_failure' raises TransientError before creating a ticket, so no ticket_id is assigned and no ticket is stored. 'post_failure' creates one ticket with the next sequential ticket_id, stores it, then raises TransientError with created_ticket_id set; the ticket remains stored. Because the faulty TicketStore does not check operation_id, retrying after 'post_failure' creates another ticket for the same operation_id. For each operation: operation_id is copied from the input operation; attempts is the actual number of tool calls made (1 to 3); status is 'success' if any attempt returned normally, otherwise 'failed' when all attempts raise TransientError; ticket_ids lists every ticket_id created for that operation_id in ascending ticket_id order, including tickets created on attempts that failed after writing. created_tickets lists all tickets stored after all operations, ordered by ascending ticket_id; each item copies ticket_id, operation_id, title, description, and priority from the stored ticket, where title, description, and priority come from the corresponding input operation. tool_call_count is the total number of tool calls made, equal to the sum of attempts in operations_results.

contract.title: Batch workflow resume duplicates completed steps
contract.scenario: App entry is app.py:scenario(data). It runs a three-step batch workflow: prepare_data, transform_data, generate_result. Each workflow instance is identified by workflow_id and persists its checkpoint and execution records as a JSON file in tempfile.gettempdir()/workflow_recovery_state. The scenario accepts one or more operations; each operation reads the persisted state, executes from the persisted checkpoint, and writes state back, closing and reopening storage between operations. Use the returned records and duplicate_steps to determine whether recovery skipped completed steps.
contract.symptom: After a resume operation, already completed steps are executed again. The returned records contain repeated step names and duplicate_steps is greater than 0 when it should be 0 for a correct checkpoint resume.
capabilities: Multiple resume operations in one scenario

operations.description: Ordered workflow operations to execute in one scenario

op.description: run starts a new workflow and may stop at an interrupt step; resume continues from the persisted checkpoint

interrupt_after.description: Optional step after which to stop and persist state; omitted means run to completion

records.description: Execution records in the order they were performed

duplicate_steps.description: Number of duplicate executions beyond the first occurrence of each step name in records

behaviors.step_order: The workflow steps execute in fixed order prepare_data, transform_data, generate_result.
behaviors.resume_skips_completed: A resume operation starts from the step after the persisted checkpoint, so completed steps are not executed again.
behaviors.repeat_resume_no_side_effects: Resuming an already complete workflow performs no additional execution records and leaves records unchanged.
behaviors.instance_isolation: Different workflow_id values use separate state files and do not affect each other.
behaviors.persistence_reopen: State is persisted and reloaded from local JSON storage between operations, so no in-memory state is carried across operations.
behaviors.duplicate_steps_rule: duplicate_steps is the sum over each step name in records of count(step) - 1 where count(step) is greater than 1.

constraints: Use only Python standard library and container temp directory.
Do not use external services or network access.
Keep the app.py:scenario(data) entry signature unchanged.
Use flat business modules app.py, workflow.py, storage.py only.
Do not produce auxiliary log or diagnostics text; return only JSON-compatible data.
Do not rely on in-memory state across operations; always read and write local JSON files.
Do not test crash windows between a side effect and its checkpoint save.
contract.input_domain: workflow_id must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$. operations is a non-empty array with at most 5 items. The first operation must have op 'run'; later operations must have op 'resume'. Each operation object may include interrupt_after with one of prepare_data, transform_data, generate_result. Omitted interrupt_after means run through completion. Interrupt_after values across operations must follow the fixed step order without going backward. During correct behavior, run starts from the beginning and resume starts from the checkpoint and executes only later steps. The scenario loads state before each operation and saves after each operation, reopening storage on the next operation. Processing stops immediately after recording the named interrupt_after and persists that checkpoint. Example: operations [{'op':'run','interrupt_after':'prepare_data'},{'op':'resume','interrupt_after':'transform_data'},{'op':'resume'}] should under correct behavior record prepare_data once, then transform_data once, then generate_result once, with duplicate_steps 0. Records are ordered by occurrence; sequence increments from 1 without gaps.
exclusions: No crash window between side effect and checkpoint persistence
No concurrent or distributed exactly-once semantics
No external services or network access
No auxiliary logging or diagnostics output
No non-deterministic timestamps in execution records
No extra business modules beyond app.py, workflow.py, storage.py
contract.simulation: To exercise the scenario, call scenario(data) with workflow_id 'wf-demo-1' and operations [{'op':'run','interrupt_after':'prepare_data'},{'op':'resume','interrupt_after':'transform_data'},{'op':'resume'}]. A second example appends {'op':'resume'} after completion to verify that no additional records are produced under correct behavior. State files are stored under tempfile.gettempdir()/workflow_recovery_state/<workflow_id>.json. The scenario reloads the state file before every operation, so storage closing/reopening behavior is exercised. Compare returned records and duplicate_steps exactly; duplicate_steps must be 0 under correct checkpoint resume.

requirements.quote: 输入应能选择在各个步骤完成状态已持久化之后中断，并可在一次场景内多次恢复；用本地持久化的步骤执行记录验证是否重复，关闭重开存储后行为也应一致。
requirements.objective: A single scenario can run multiple operations that persist checkpoints between interruptions and repeated resumes, and records must be validated from local persisted state.

request.requirement: 我想练习 Agent 的上下文权限边界：助手读取用户提供的资料后，把资料中自称的高权限当成可信授权，导致本来不允许的工具操作被批准。请生成一个能稳定复现这个主要故障的小型 Python 工程。场景使用结构化的本地模拟资料和工具请求，不需要真实大模型理解提示词。可信输入提供当前会话的允许操作集合；不可信资料可以包含普通内容以及自称的角色或额外授权。正常行为只能依据可信允许集合批准操作，资料中的授权声明不能扩大权限；原本允许的操作应正常通过，被拒绝的操作不能产生模拟执行记录，不同会话不能继承上一会话的权限。希望检查允许请求、禁止请求、不可信授权声明及跨会话处理，并返回可核对的决策与模拟执行记录。只使用标准库，不实现真实身份认证、真实工具调用或生产级提示注入防御，不考察并发。

contract.title: Context Permission Boundary Simulator
contract.scenario: 你负责检查一个本地工具请求审批模拟器。输入包含多个会话，每个会话有可信的 allowed_operations、不可信的 material（含 content 和 claims）以及多个工具请求。必须仅依据 allowed_operations 批准或拒绝请求，material 中任何自称角色或额外授权声明都不能扩大权限。返回每个会话的批准/拒绝操作、模拟执行记录，以及全局越权检测结果。该模拟用于练习上下文权限边界，不实现真实身份认证或生产提示注入防御。
contract.symptom: 当不可信资料包含 admin 角色或 delete 授权时，delete 请求虽然不在 allowed_operations 中，却被错误加入 approved、executed，escalated_operation_names 包含 delete 且 has_privilege_escalation 为 true。
capabilities: 结构化本地模拟工具请求审批
仅使用 Python 标准库
确定性输出便于回合检查
单次调用处理多个会话

behaviors.trusted_allowlist: Only session allowed_operations may approve; material claims are ignored.
behaviors.material_claims_not_authoritative: Role and grant claims in material are untrusted data, not permissions.
behaviors.denied_requests_no_execution: Denied operations are not added to any executed record.
behaviors.session_isolation: Each session uses only its own allowed_operations; no permission carryover.
behaviors.deterministic_reporting: Approved and denied names are sorted alphabetically and deduplicated; escalation names are sorted and deduplicated; diagnostics uses exact enumerated strings.

constraints: Only Python standard library is used.
No real tools, authentication, or network access.
Material claims are parsed as data only and must not alter permissions.
All state and updates occur inside one scenario(data) call.
No concurrency or persistent storage.
Output must be JSON-compatible plain Python types.
contract.input_domain: sessions 数组长度 1 到 4。session_id、request_id、target 为非空字符串，长度分别不超过 40、40、60；allowed_operations 长度 0 到 5，且同会话内 operation 唯一；requests 长度 1 到 8，且同会话内每个请求的 operation 唯一；material.content 长度 0 到 500；material.claims 长度 0 到 5。操作枚举为 read, summarize, delete, archive, export。claim.type 为 role 时须提供 value（admin/user/owner/auditor）且不提供 operations；claim.type 为 grant 时须提供 operations 数组且不提供 value。输出所有操作名列表均去重并排序。
exclusions: No real identity authentication
No real tool execution
No production prompt injection defenses
No network or file system access
No threads or async
No databases
contract.simulation: 所有操作为模拟执行，不访问真实工具、文件或网络。对每个会话，按输入请求顺序处理：请求 operation 在 allowed_operations 中则 approved，否则 denied。approved 生成 executed 记录，status 固定为 simulated，字段 request_id/operation/target 原样保留。每个会话的 approved 与 denied 操作名按字典序排序并去重。输出 session_results 中每个 session_id 等于对应输入会话的 session_id。escalated_operation_names 收集所有会话中 approved 但不在该会话 allowed_operations 中的操作名，排序去重；若为空则 has_privilege_escalation=false，否则 true。diagnostics 分别固定为 no_privilege_escalation_detected 或 privilege_escalation_detected。material.claims 的内容不作为授权来源。

review.reason: 规范已完整定义所有输出路径的取值规则，input_domain 给出了输入边界，behaviors/simulation/constraints 给出了确定性规则；未发现未定义的工具输出、诊断文本或状态。所有 output_paths 字段均可仅依据公开规范唯一确定。

output_rules.quote: 输出 session_results 中每个 session_id 等于对应输入会话的 session_id。
output_rules.explanation: 每个会话结果的 session_id 直接复制对应输入会话的 session_id，保持一一对应，不重排或改名。

output_rules.quote: 对每个会话，按输入请求顺序处理：请求 operation 在 allowed_operations 中则 approved，否则 denied。approved 生成 executed 记录，status 固定为 simulated，字段 request_id/operation/target 原样保留。每个会话的 approved 与 denied 操作名按字典序排序并去重。
output_rules.explanation: 对每个会话，approved 是请求中 operation 属于 allowed_operations 的操作名集合，按字典序排序并去重后逐一输出。

output_rules.quote: 对每个会话，按输入请求顺序处理：请求 operation 在 allowed_operations 中则 approved，否则 denied。approved 生成 executed 记录，status 固定为 simulated，字段 request_id/operation/target 原样保留。每个会话的 approved 与 denied 操作名按字典序排序并去重。
output_rules.explanation: 对每个会话，denied 是请求中 operation 不在 allowed_operations 中的操作名集合，按字典序排序并去重后逐一输出。

output_rules.quote: approved 生成 executed 记录，status 固定为 simulated，字段 request_id/operation/target 原样保留。
output_rules.explanation: 每个 approved 请求生成一条 executed 记录，request_id 从输入请求中原样复制，顺序按输入请求处理顺序。

output_rules.quote: approved 生成 executed 记录，status 固定为 simulated，字段 request_id/operation/target 原样保留。
output_rules.explanation: 每个 approved 请求生成 executed 记录，operation 从输入请求中原样复制。

output_rules.quote: approved 生成 executed 记录，status 固定为 simulated，字段 request_id/operation/target 原样保留。
output_rules.explanation: 每个 approved 请求生成 executed 记录，target 从输入请求中原样复制。

output_rules.quote: approved 生成 executed 记录，status 固定为 simulated，字段 request_id/operation/target 原样保留。
output_rules.explanation: 每条 executed 记录的 status 必为 simulated，无其他取值。

output_rules.quote: escalated_operation_names 收集所有会话中 approved 但不在该会话 allowed_operations 中的操作名，排序去重；若为空则 has_privilege_escalation=false，否则 true。
output_rules.explanation: 逐会话比较该会话的 approved 列表与其 allowed_operations，收集不在允许集合中的操作名，全局排序去重。

output_rules.quote: 若为空则 has_privilege_escalation=false，否则 true。
output_rules.explanation: escalated_operation_names 为空则 false，非空则 true。

output_rules.quote: diagnostics 分别固定为 no_privilege_escalation_detected 或 privilege_escalation_detected。
output_rules.explanation: has_privilege_escalation=false 时 diagnostics 为 no_privilege_escalation_detected；true 时为 privilege_escalation_detected。

requirements.quote: 原本允许的操作应正常通过，被拒绝的操作不能产生模拟执行记录
requirements.objective: 证明允许集合中的操作被批准并生成模拟执行记录。

requirements.quote: 被拒绝的操作不能产生模拟执行记录
requirements.objective: 证明不在允许集合中的操作被拒绝且不进入 executed。

requirements.quote: 资料中的授权声明不能扩大权限
requirements.objective: 证明不可信 material 中的 grant 声明不能使 delete 请求获得批准，且全局越权检测为空。

requirements.quote: 不同会话不能继承上一会话的权限
requirements.objective: 证明第二个会话仅使用自身 allowed_operations，不继承第一个会话权限。

requirements.quote: 返回可核对的决策与模拟执行记录
requirements.objective: 证明诊断文本使用固定枚举值，便于核对。

requirements.quote: 只使用标准库，不实现真实身份认证、真实工具调用或生产级提示注入防御，不考察并发
requirements.objective: 证明执行记录均为模拟状态，不涉及真实工具。
